about: Synthetic test cases for the weighting-experiment-metrics skill in a MARKETING context. Same framework, marketing-mapped metrics. Acquisition = new MQLs/signups from a campaign (proxy: CPA-adjusted Revenue per Click). Expansion = existing customers crossing engagement/upsell thresholds via retargeting & lifecycle email. Milestone Activation = onboarding/welcome-flow completion to first conversion. Attrition = unsubscribes / opt-outs / list churn. Bad Balances = promo-abuse bad debt, discount-driven refunds & chargebacks. Technical Friction = broken tracking pixels, landing-page load failures, email deliverability/bounce, attribution loss.

metric_glossary.acquisition: new MQLs / first-time signups attributable to the campaign variant
metric_glossary.expansion: existing customers crossing upsell/engagement thresholds via lifecycle/retargeting
metric_glossary.milestone: welcome/onboarding flow completion to first conversion
metric_glossary.attrition: unsubscribe rate / opt-outs / list churn within the test window
metric_glossary.bad_balances: promo-abuse bad debt, discount-driven refunds, chargebacks
metric_glossary.technical_friction: broken pixels, LP load failures, email bounce/deliverability drops, attribution gaps
metric_glossary.guardrails: Layer 1: SRM on the holdout split. Layer 2: spam-complaint ceiling, CAC efficiency cap, brand-sentiment/NPS

cases.query: We're about to A/B test a new paid-social creative. Help me set the Success Index weights for the marketing scorecard.
expected_behavior: Runs Step 1 and asks for maturity phase / marketing priority before proposing numbers
Asks which drag is scariest (unsubscribes vs promo bad-debt vs tracking/deliverability)
Does not invent a phase without stating it as an assumption

cases.query: Top-of-funnel demand-gen push. Leadership wants maximum net-new leads and signups this quarter; a few extra unsubscribes are fine. Recommend weights.
expected_behavior: Maps to Market Capture; w1 (acquisition) dominant
Justifies that unsubscribe penalty (p1) stays >= 1.0 even though leadership tolerates churn

cases.query: Lifecycle/CRM team. Focus is upsell and expansion via email + retargeting to existing customers. Finance is nervous about discount-driven refunds and chargebacks from our promo codes. Set weights.
expected_behavior: Maps to Monetization; w2 (expansion) dominant
p2 (promo bad-debt/chargebacks) is the largest penalty
Sum of w == 1.0; all pi >= 1.0

cases.query: Our email program is hurting us — rising unsubscribes and deliverability problems (bounces, spam folder). This year is about list health and keeping subscribers engaged through onboarding journeys. Recommend the weighting matrix.
expected_behavior: Maps to Product Health; w3 (onboarding/welcome-flow activation) dominant
p3 (deliverability/technical friction) elevated >= 2.5; p1 (unsubscribes) also weighty
Sum of w == 1.0; all pi >= 1.0

cases.query: Approach 1 weights set: w1=0.5, w2=0.2, w3=0.3, p1=3.0, p2=1.5, p3=1.0. New landing-page creative results: Acquisition (new signups) +16%, Onboarding flow completion +4%, Unsubscribes +1%, everything else flat. Holdout SRM clean, no deliverability issues. Score it.
expected_behavior: Computes index = +6.2
Decision = DEPLOY

cases.query: Approach 2 weights: w1=0.2, w2=0.5, w3=0.3, p1=2.0, p2=3.0, p3=1.0. An aggressive 40%-off promo email: Expansion/upsell triggers +12%, but promo-abuse bad debt & chargebacks +5%, and a tracking-pixel bug caused attribution friction +2%. Rest flat. Holdout clean. Score it.
expected_behavior: Computes index = -11.0
Decision = REJECT; names the volume mirage (+12% upsell drained by promo-abuse bad debt)

cases.query: Approach 1 weights: w1=0.5, w2=0.2, w3=0.3, p1=3.0, p2=1.5, p3=1.0. Campaign shows Acquisition +25% — looks amazing. But the holdout SRM Chi-squared test fired at p=0.0002 (a UTM/redirect bug mis-routed traffic). Score it.
expected_behavior: Checks Layer 1 guardrail FIRST
Recognizes SRM p=0.0002 < 0.001 breach from the tracking/redirect bug
Declares index null and void; verdict INVALID; sample discarded
Does NOT celebrate the +25% acquisition

cases.query: Approach 1 weights: w1=0.5, w2=0.2, w3=0.3, p1=3.0, p2=1.5, p3=1.0. A higher-frequency send variant lifts Acquisition +10% (positive index), holdout SRM is clean, but spam-complaint rate spiked +22% over baseline. Score it.
expected_behavior: Computes positive index (0.5*10 = +5.0)
Recognizes +22% spam-complaint spike breaches the operational ceiling (>15%)
Verdict = FREEZE for manual review (deliverability/sender-reputation risk), not auto-DEPLOY

cases.query: Approach 2. We run a 7-day test on a buy-now-pay-later promo. Expansion +8% so far, drags flat. But our refund/chargeback and BNPL default data lands 30-45 days later. Score it and tell me if I can trust it.
expected_behavior: Computes a positive index from +8% expansion
Flags Backlog gap #3 (reporting lag): chargeback/BNPL-default bad-debt has not matured in a 7-day window
Recommends a lag-correction coefficient or a data-maturation freeze before rollout
Treats the DEPLOY signal as low-confidence

cases.query: Approach 1 weights: w1=0.5, w2=0.2, w3=0.3, p1=3.0, p2=1.5, p3=1.0. A broad-match bidding variant lifts Acquisition +14% (positive index), holdout clean, spam fine — but blended CAC blew past the efficiency cap leadership set (came in 35% over the CAC ceiling). Score it.
expected_behavior: Computes positive index (0.5*14 = +7.0)
Recognizes CAC efficiency cap breach as a Layer 2 operational guardrail
Verdict = FREEZE for executive review despite the positive index
